metadata.title: Cedar Rapids Community School Dist. v. Garret F., 526 U.S. 66 (1999) (No. 96-1793)
metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: Cedar Rapids Community School Dist. v. Garret F.

Opinion filed: 1999-06-01

Docket No.: 96-1793

Citations:
• 143 L. Ed. 2d 154
• 119 S. Ct. 992
• 526 U.S. 66
• 1999 U.S. LEXIS 1709

Case holding summaries:
• noting medical services exception limited to those services that must be performed by a physician
• Nursing service was necessary for a quadriplegic student.
• "As a general matter, services that enable a disabled child to remain in school during the day provide the student with `the meaningful access to education that Congress envisioned.'" (citation omitted)
• “Continuous services may be more costly and may require additional school personnel, but they are not thereby more ‘medical.’”
• "the term `medical services' refer[s] only to services that must be performed by a physician, and not to school health services"
• dealing with the need for a ventilator for a wheelchair-bound student to keep him alive
• whether the services required for access to a FAPE constituted an unfair financial burden to the school district
